verdict.rationale: Fenwick keeps a dedicated 'artificial-intelligence-tools' service-innovation page. It describes specific AI uses in client work: uploading a brief so the tool surfaces uncited relevant cases, and automating contract-provision extraction and summaries for due diligence. Fenwick Labs separately documents in-house client-facing products such as automated incorporation documents and intelligent patent alerts. This goes beyond a bare marketing mention, but the quoted evidence does not name the AI tools and publishes no AI-use policy or governance. missing for 10: named AI tools/vendors, a published AI use or governance policy, confirmation that Fenwick Labs products are AI-driven, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the firm publishes how it uses AI in client service — named tools, policies, or AI-practice products of its own — beyond a marketing mention

citations.quote: Lawyers simply upload a legal brief into the interface, which then quickly identifies highly relevant cases that are not cited in the brief.
Its search capabilities were designed for due diligence review and can automate the extraction and analysis of key contract provisions and create summaries in seconds.
Whether it's automated generation of incorporation documents for new startups, intelligent alerts for Patent clients
